global_caption: The video consists of four shots and features a guzheng solo performance in a low-saturation watercolor illustration style. The overall color palette gradually transitions from the cool, soft blue-gray of early morning to the warm golden hues of dusk.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, wide overhead composition establishing the forest clearing and the path leading to the mountain top. Foreground features softly blurred foliage, central focus is a big-eyed fairy carrying a guzheng walking toward a wooden platform in the woods. The frame retains delicate watercolor paper-like soft edges. Morning mist and dappled forest light create a quiet, transparent atmosphere. The fairy climbs onto the platform, gently places the guzheng, sits down, and tests the strings with a few plucks. Her clothing and hair tips flutter slightly in the morning breeze. shot3: Eye-level slightly upward angle includes winding stone steps, flanking trees, and distant rising terrain. Occasional foreground grass blades sweep across the frame as leading lines. The subject remains slightly off-center. The fairy carries the guzheng while walking and playing. The performance evolves from gentle plucking to more fluid hook-press-roll techniques, forming a progression from seated to mobile performance. shot4: Shot 4 uses a brief fade-in/fade-out transition from the previous shot to a close-up at the mountain top. Frame is a close-up with slight upward angle, compressing the fairy, upper half of the guzheng, and the swirling twilight sea of clouds into one layer. Backlight from the side-rear outlines her silhouette. Overall texture maintains low-saturation watercolor quality, with only warm gold accents on cloud edges and wood grain. The fairy sits on a wooden bench completing the final roll technique. Her shoulders relax slightly, eyes fall to the instrument surface. Fingers move from dense to sparse, strong to light. During the extended final note, string resonance visibly diminishes. A faint wooden creak from the bench occurs as her weight shifts slightly downward, naturally overlapping with the last note. The camera slowly pushes in to frame both face and hands, then gently stops, letting the quiet expression in the sunset and the final string release become the ending. The image fades out with the last trace of the guzheng tone.
